Caterpillar (CAT): business-model profile, energy/power mode (Josh, 26 October 2026). Sources: 2025 10-K, 4Q25, 1Q26 and 2Q26 releases and analyst decks, 2Q26 10-Q, XBRL company facts.

1) Economic engine. Caterpillar sells machines, engines, gensets and turbines through 150 independent dealers and earns a long services tail. It returns substantially all MP&E free cash flow, while Cat Financial funds customer purchases (10-K; 1Q26 deck).

2) Revenue map. Since 2026 there are three primary segments: Construction Industries, Resource Industries (now including Rail) and Power & Energy (recast 8-K, 26 March 2026), plus Financial Products. Power & Energy revenue = units ordered x price per kW (reciprocating gensets up to 10 MW; Solar turbines 1 to 39 MW, Titan 350 up to 38 MW) plus services. Power & Energy 2025 sales were $28.6bn, with external sales split 43% Power Generation, 32% Oil & Gas and 25% Industrial (P&E deck, September 2026). 2Q26: Power & Energy $8,238mn, Power Generation $3,098mn (up 29%). Backlog was $72.1bn, with 59% due within 12 months. Services were $24bn in 2025 against a $30bn target for 2030.

3) Cost structure. Steel and components, tariffs (about $2.2bn guided for 2026, excluding IEEPA recoveries), depreciation on capacity additions, R&D and restructuring ($300mn to $350mn in 2026).

4) Capital and funding. MP&E capex is about $3.5bn in 2026, and the 2030 target is 4% to 5% of MP&E sales. Capacity goals versus 2024: large reciprocating engines nearly 3x, turbines 2.5x. The MP&E free cash flow target range is $6bn to $15bn. At 30 June 2026, MP&E debt was $10,690mn and Cat Financial debt was $34,456mn (match-funded). Credit lines of $11.5bn were undrawn (8-K, 1 September 2026).

5) Sensitivities. Data center capex and siting rules; price realization against tariffs; capacity ramp timing; dealer inventory; mining and construction cycles; Cat Financial credit losses.

6) Competitive position. Largest installed base and dealer network. Named competitors include Cummins, Rolls-Royce Power Systems and Siemens Energy (10-K). Gas prime gensets are sold out into late 2028; turbines run longer.

7) What would break it. Data center orders stall or cancel; local moratoria spread; capacity arrives as demand peaks and price falls; tariffs outpace price; vendor financing (as on the 2 GW AIP deal) brings developer credit losses to Cat Financial.
